group: base-5 counter of gadgets + growing block
title: What is known about 1RB1LF_1LC0RD_0LD0LC_1RE0LA_0RA0RC_0RE---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LF_1LC0RD_0LD0LC_1RE0LA_0RA0RC_0RE---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the passes of the base-5 counter (each phase of the first gadget, and a carry into the second); the round ends follow a radix-5 pattern seen in simulation, but the step from one round end to the next, where blocks run out and are rebuilt, is not derived, so halting is not reduced to a map.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 86,722 cells have been visited and 22,504 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.525). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.057).

claims.title: The sweeps
claims.text: Sixteen shift rules over (10)^n, (01)^n, (1000)^n and the rotations of these words, for all n and any tapes around (one copy by rfl, all copies by TM.cross_r / TM.cross_l).

claims.title: Right-end events to 2.9·10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: A C run to 2.9·1010 steps, sampled each time the tape grows on the right (24 times): the tape is a list of blocks a^x (a = 10) separated by 1^2 0. In the last samples block j from the right loses 18·5j−1 copies of a between events.

claims.title: The counter passes
claims.text: With b = 1000 and the gadgets G0 = 10010, G1 = 1001, G2 = 1001100, G3 = 100110, G4 = 10011: one pass of the head from the left end ticks the first gadget, G0→G1 and G1→G2 moving one b from the block after it to the block before it, G2→G3, G3→G4 moving nothing, and the left block gains a b; G4→G0 carries into the next gadget, which ticks the same way (or, if it is a fresh 0, becomes G1). Nine theorems, for all block lengths ≥ 3.

claims.title: Round ends to 4.8·10<sup>13</sup> steps
claims.text: At each round end (the head at the right end of the tape) the tape is ax1 1 ax2 1 … axk 1 aL with a = 10; L is 311 since step 4.2·109. From one round end to the next the block j places left of L loses 18·5j−1 a's while it can pay; blocks that cannot pay are rebuilt or merged, and new leftmost blocks have length 12·5m−4 (37,496, 187,496, 937,496, 4,687,496). 31 round ends found.

claims.title: No halt in 2.4·10<sup>14</sup> steps
claims.text: An exact accelerated simulator (the macro machine of bbtools.macro with 4-cell blocks, plus jumps over repeated periods of passes) runs 2.4·1014 steps in 15 minutes without a halt. It agrees with the plain C simulator on the whole tape (a hash) at 107, 109, 5·109 and 1010 steps; the jumps themselves are not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A halt needs 1 A> 1; the counter passes never produce it, so it would have to come from a block running out or from the re-encoding at a round end, which are not derived yet.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine is a counter in base 5: gadgets between blocks of 1000s are its digits, the head's passes are what it counts, and every tick is paid for by moving a 1000 from one block to the next. Lean proves the passes; what happens when a block runs out is the open part.

facts.text: Passes and carries of the base-5 counter, for all block lengths.
No halt in an exact accelerated simulation.
What block j pays per round, seen at 31 round ends.

sections.heading: A counter in base 5
html:
Write b for 1000. During a round the tape is bn G1 bm1 G2 bm2 …: blocks of b's with a gadget between neighbours. A gadget is a digit in base 5, one of five short words:

digitworda tick from this digit
010010moves one b from the block after the gadget to the block before it
11001the same
21001100nothing moves
3100110nothing moves
410011back to 0, and carry: the next gadget ticks

The head bounces between the left end and the first gadget; each pass ticks it once and adds a b to the left block. So the gadgets count the passes in base 5, and block j pays two b's per cycle of gadget j while receiving two per cycle of gadget j+1. Lean proves the four passes and the carries (lean/Counter.lean).

sections.heading: Radix-5 payments
html:
When every gadget carries, the head runs to the right end of the tape and the list is written with a = 10: ax1 1 ax2 1 … aL. From one round end to the next the block j places left of the last block pays 18·5j−1 a's:

sections.heading: Where a halt could come from
html: The machine stops only on F reading 1, which needs 1 A> 1. The counter's passes never do that, for any block lengths. A halt would have to come from a block running out, or from the re-encoding between b's and a's at a round end; neither step has been derived yet, so the question is open. An exact accelerated simulator ran 2.4·1014 steps without a halt.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.525). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.057).
After 109 steps the tape spans 86,722 cells (53,224 left of the start, 52 right), with a density of 1s of 0.259.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A base-5 counter: five-phase gadgets between blocks of 1000s count the passes of the head, each tick paid for by moving 1000s between blocks; passes and carries proved in Lean, round ends follow radix-5 decrements 18·5^(j−1); no halt in 2.4·10^14 steps; open.
